english.title: Dishonestly sub-let / part with possession of dwelling-house let under secure tenancy in breach of a term of the tenancy

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: prevention of social housing fraud act 2013

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a tenant of a dwelling-house let under a secure tenancy, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ADDRESS..), dishonestly and in breach of an express or implied term of the tenancy,

(A)_[sub-let]_
(B)_[parted with possession of]_

(C)_[the whole of the dwelling-house]_
(D)_[part of the dwelling-house, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PART OF THE HOUSE..), without the landlord's written consent]_

and ceased to occupy the dwelling-house as your only or principal home
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(2) and (6) of the Prevention of Social Housing Fraud Act 2013.

Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Where there is no element of 'dishonesty' on the part of the tenant, offence document H11400 should be used.
(ii) An unlawful profit order may be made by a court in relation to a defendant convicted of this offence - see section 4 of the Act for further details.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
Notes
(i) The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates' court, see section 1(6)(a) of the Prevention of Social Housing Fraud Act 2013 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
(ii) On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
